utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC
utterances.text: That is Sustjepan. It is a slope, a geographic term.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us: How wide is this water dividing Mokosica and Sustjepan?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC
utterances.text: I said it was about 300 metres. It's not the same everywhere, but it's between 250 to 300 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Were the Croat military positions located in Sustjepan?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was there any fire or provocation coming from there towards Mokosica?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mostly it came from there. Most of the provocations came from there, although fire was not opened from the command post. Actually, they did not open fire at the command post; only at the vehicles moving along that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Could you please show us the road Mokosica-Lozica-Slano, that road that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC
utterances.text: Zatun [phoen], Veliki, Mali. That is that main highway, main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was the supply of Mokosica conducted along that road? Did the supply vehicles use that communication in order to bring supplies to Mokosica?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC
utterances.text: That was the only road that they used. There was no other road.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you ever personally go along that road from Mokosica towards Slano?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC
utterances.text: Yes, frequently. I mostly used two motor vehicles, one larger motor vehicle that would go along the coast, and I would go -- travel alongside it so that I would not be exposed to fire from the Croat side.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So that motor vehicle, if we are looking in the direction of Mokosica, Slano, that would be facing Sustjepan and the sea?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC
utterances.text: And my vehicle would be on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And that was because of the firing from this side where the Croatian forces were?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object. It's leading. I've let most of the leading go, but it's just continuing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. I think you could be a little more careful there, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll do my best, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Djurasic: Apart from these provocations, this opening of fire on the road that you spoke of, were there any other problems related to security and safety on that road?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC
utterances.text: Well, I would mostly focus on that. That road was not under my jurisdiction in its entirety, so I am only speaking of the section of the road where I was and where there were various points.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please: At the Mokosica command, what kind of communication did you have with the outside world, that is to say, the world out of Mokosica?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC
utterances.text: I had telephone communications with the forward command post of the 9th VPS, and I had communication with Dubrovnik, telephone communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: May I just interrupt you at this point. When you say that you had communication with the forward command post of the 9th VPS, was this some kind of a military communication, civilian? Could you describe it.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC
utterances.text: It was a military wire connection.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is that some kind of a telephone or what is it?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC
utterances.text: It's a telephone. It's an inductor telephone, a military telephone. It is not an automatic PTT telephone. It is a military telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me: This telephone that you say that you had direct telephone line with Dubrovnik, what kind of a line was that?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC
utterances.text: This was established in a different period. I didn't have it at the outset. It was during the second half of my stay there. When we started communications or contacts with certain people, like Mr. Simunovic, from Dubrovnik, then we established this telephone connection so that we could communicate and regulate precisely traffic on these roads around Rijeka Dubrovacka, for the sake of their transportation and ours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, specifically: This communication with Dubrovnik, is this a telephone also or is it a radio device?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC
utterances.text: A telephone, a PTT telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: When you say "PTT," that is civilian?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC
utterances.text: Yes, civilian. The existing telephone lines with the number that was already there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you use that telephone often, this telephone connection with Dubrovnik, in order to possibly carry out cooperation with the other side?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC
utterances.text: Well, you cannot say that it was frequent, but we would talk a few times a week, and if there were a problem that cropped up, then we would speak again. There was no set routine.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me: In that period, was there any kind of navigation towards Mokosica?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC
utterances.text: In the first period of time, no. It started functioning only in 1992, in January, February, when conditions were created from a security point of view for the unhindered travel of these people to and from Dubrovnik. Then it started every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: A few minutes, if I'm not mistaken, you mentioned the name of Ivo Simunovic from Dubrovnik; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us a bit more about who this is?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC
utterances.text: Ivo Simunovic introduced himself over the telephone to me as the representative of the defence of the town of Dubrovnik, who wished to meet me personally at a given point in time so that we could discuss the security conditions, the opening of fire, and so on. And I suggested to him that he come to my command post, which he accepted. He came - I cannot say exactly - two or three times to my command post. We had meetings. We discussed all these problems. For example, one characteristic case was when international observers came from an international organisation, and he led them. They were on the right side of the Rijeka Dubrovacka and he called me and asked that there not be any provocations from our side, so that he could have free passage there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: When he came to see you, what did he wear?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO DJURASIC
utterances.text: He wore a uniform. A military uniform of the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, is the time right for us to adjourn now and continue tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that is so, Mr. Rodic. We commence tomorrow at 11.00, I believe. There was a medical appointment that had to be accommodated earlier in the day. So we adjourn now until 11.00. Mr. Djurasic, we must ask you to adjourn tomorrow and your evidence will continue at 11.00 in the morning.
